# Getting Started

## Prerequisites

- [ ] [Claude Code CLI](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code) installed and authenticated
- [ ] Git installed — **2.36 or newer** in a project that opts in to spec claims (`docs/spec-claims/`): a claims check over a commit range that holds a merge reads its hand resolutions with `git show --remerge-diff`, and an older git makes that check indeterminate (exit 2)
- [ ] bash **3.2 or newer** — macOS's `/bin/bash` is enough; nothing needs bash 4
- [ ] `jq` **1.6 or newer** installed (`brew install jq` / `apt install jq`) — required by bundled freshness tooling, which refuses an older jq
- [ ] `sha256sum` (Linux) or `shasum` (macOS) — one of them; the bundled tooling refuses to run with neither
- [ ] A project to document (any language, any framework)

Optional:
- [ ] Mermaid MCP server configured (for PNG diagram rendering)
- [ ] [`gh`](https://cli.github.com), authenticated — only for the work ledger's GitHub adapters (`doc-superpowers:ledger-pr-gh`, `doc-superpowers:ledger-items-gh`) and `ledger init --sources github`

## Installation

### Option 1: Plugin marketplace (Recommended)

In Claude Code, add this repository as a plugin marketplace, then install the plugin from it:

```
/plugin marketplace add woodrowpearson/doc-superpowers
/plugin install doc-superpowers@doc-superpowers
```

### Option 2: Clone and Symlink

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone git@github.com:woodrowpearson/doc-superpowers.git ~/code/doc-superpowers

# Symlink into Claude Code skills directory
ln -s ~/code/doc-superpowers ~/.claude/skills/doc-superpowers
```

This approach lets you pull updates with `git pull` and track local modifications. Claude Code loads the symlinked folder as the plugin `doc-superpowers@skills-dir` (see the [README](../../README.md#claude-code)).

### Option 3: Direct Copy

```bash
# Copy into your skills directory
cp -R path/to/doc-superpowers ~/.claude/skills/doc-superpowers
```

### Verify Installation

Start a Claude Code session and check that the skill appears:

```
# The skill should show in available skills list
# You can invoke it with:
/doc-superpowers init
```

For installation in other frameworks (Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI), see the [README](../../README.md#installation).

## Configuration

No configuration required for the doc suite. Spec claims and the work ledger are opt-in, and need some: see [Spec lifecycle commands](#spec-lifecycle-commands) and [Work ledger (opt-in)](#work-ledger-opt-in). The skill auto-detects everything it needs from the target project.

**Optional enhancements** the skill will auto-discover if present:

| Enhancement | How to Add | What It Enables |
|-------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Mermaid MCP | `claude mcp add` (`--scope user` for every project; `--scope project` writes `.mcp.json` at the project root, shared through git) | PNG diagram rendering instead of inline source |

Bundled: `scripts/doc-tools.sh` provides freshness tracking out of the box — content hashing for docs, content identity for code (the git object id of each code ref, recorded when a doc is indexed or re-baselined). No additional scripts needed.

## First Run

### Generate docs for a new project

```bash
cd your-project/
# Start Claude Code
claude

# Generate full documentation suite
/doc-superpowers init
```

This will:
1. Discover your project's structure, tech stack, and existing tooling
2. Generate docs in `docs/` (architecture, workflows, codebase guide, conventions, getting started, and the spec and ADR indexes with their templates), plus the docs each detected scope adds (the *Scope → Generated Docs Matrix* in `skills/doc-superpowers/SKILL.md`)
3. Create or update `CLAUDE.md` (and sync `README.md`, if you have one)
4. Mark each generated file except the `template.md` files (a spec or ADR copied from one would inherit a false marker) with `<!-- Generated by doc-superpowers -->`, and index every generated doc in `docs/.doc-index.json`, the freshness record
5. Offer to commit, then check that every generated doc reads `current`
6. Suggest installing workflow hooks for automated freshness monitoring

If you ask for a work ledger (or `docs/ledger/config.json` already exists), it also bootstraps one before the commit, with your review of the proposed ledgers and assignments — see [Work ledger (opt-in)](#work-ledger-opt-in).

### Install workflow hooks (recommended follow-up)

After `init` completes, set up automated freshness monitoring:

```bash
# Install all three hook tiers (git, Claude Code, CI/CD) — not the work ledger's sets
/doc-superpowers hooks install --all

# Or pick specific tiers
/doc-superpowers hooks install --git           # Git hooks only
/doc-superpowers hooks install --claude        # Claude Code hooks only (per-user)
/doc-superpowers hooks install --ci            # GitHub Actions: the 2 shell workflows

# Claude-powered workflows are opt-in by name
/doc-superpowers hooks install --ci --workflows=doc-release
/doc-superpowers hooks install --ci --workflows=none                 # vendor doc-tools.sh only

# With a work ledger (docs/ledger/config.json): its opt-in sets, never part of --all
/doc-superpowers hooks install --ledger        # pre-commit validate, pre-push provisional-key check, post-commit in-flight push
/doc-superpowers hooks install --ledger-claude # Claude Code: SessionStart notices, the state-watch hook (per-user)
```

The installer acts on the repository's top level from any subdirectory, puts git hooks where git runs them, keeps a hook of yours (a marked block after its `#!` line runs ours), and refuses — writing nothing — a symbolic link on a path it would write or a global or system `core.hooksPath`. The Claude tier is per-user: `.claude/settings.local.json` and `.claude/hooks/doc-superpowers/` are excluded from git through git's `info/exclude` (`git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude`, which is not `.git/info/exclude` in a linked worktree or a submodule).

**Upgrading from 2.x?** Re-run every tier you use (`/doc-superpowers hooks status` marks each hook, script or setting another version installed `⚠ … outdated`), and read the README's [Upgrading from 2.x](../../README.md#upgrading-from-2x): v2's AI workflows stay installed until you remove them, the Claude tier's files must be untracked (each teammate then re-runs `install --claude`), and design specs typed `spec` are retyped with `set-doc-type`.

The CI tier records its choices — the workflow set, `--base-branch`, `--cron`, `--ci-strict` — in `.claude/doc-superpowers/installed.json` (commit it); a plain `install --ci` reproduces them. A workflow you uninstalled with `/doc-superpowers hooks uninstall --ci --workflows=doc-release` is NOT re-added on the next no-flag `install --ci` — re-add it with `--workflows=doc-release` (explicit beats state) or `--force` (bypass state-respect). Use `--transient` on uninstall to mark "remove for now but re-add automatically next time."

Independent of hooks, you can vendor `doc-tools.sh` itself into a consumer repo. Inside a session the skill resolves the tool itself (SKILL.md, *Detect Bundled Tooling*: `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/../../scripts/doc-tools.sh`, the plugin root two directories above the skill). From a terminal, set `$DOC_TOOLS` to that same file — the path depends on how the skill was installed:

```bash
# Plugin install (Option 1) — the newest cached version, in numeric order
C=~/.claude/plugins/cache/doc-superpowers/doc-superpowers
DOC_TOOLS="$C/$(ls "$C" | grep -Ex '[0-9]+[.][0-9]+[.][0-9]+' | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n -k3,3n | tail -n 1)/scripts/doc-tools.sh"

# Clone-and-symlink or direct copy (Options 2 and 3 above)
DOC_TOOLS=~/.claude/skills/doc-superpowers/scripts/doc-tools.sh
```

Run these from the repository's top level: `tools` resolves `--dest` (default `.github/scripts`) against the current directory.

```bash
$DOC_TOOLS tools install                          # → .github/scripts/doc-tools.sh
$DOC_TOOLS tools install --dest bin --with-helpers # → bin/doc-tools.sh + bin/doc-pr-release/ + bin/doc-superpowers-steps/
$DOC_TOOLS tools install --helper ledger          # + .github/scripts/ledger/ and adapters/: the work ledger, for a vendored copy
$DOC_TOOLS tools status                            # shows location, drift + the plugin's version
```

A vendored `doc-tools.sh` runs the work ledger from `ledger/` and `adapters/` beside it: without them, every ledger verb (and, on a ledger-enabled project, the claims check V5) exits 2. `hooks install --ci` ships that set with `doc-ledger-publish` and with each workflow that runs the claims check.

Shipping the `doc-pr-release` helpers (`--with-helpers`, or `--helper doc-pr-release`) also creates `RELEASE-NOTES.next/README.md`, the fragment-format spec, when it is absent; an existing one is never overwritten.

### Audit existing docs

```bash
/doc-superpowers audit
```

This scans all docs against current code and produces a severity-ranked report (P0 Critical through P3 Style), written to `docs/plans/`. Apply it with `/doc-superpowers update --report=<that path>`.

### Review docs before a PR

```bash
/doc-superpowers review-pr
```

Maps your changed files to affected documentation and reports what needs updating.

### Draft release notes

```bash
# Draft a release notes entry from recent git history
/doc-superpowers release

# Start from a specific tag or commit
/doc-superpowers release --from=v2.2.0
```

Scans git history (from the last release — its tag, or the commit that added its `RELEASE-NOTES.md` heading when it was never tagged — or a specified `--from` ref) and drafts a semantic-versioned entry for `RELEASE-NOTES.md`. If `RELEASE-NOTES.next/PR-*.md` fragments are present (produced by the `doc-pr-release.yml` CI workflow on each open PR), the action merges every one still present into the new entry — losslessly, or it skips the fragment with a warning and keeps it for the next release — and deletes exactly the ones it consumed in the release commit. Human-edited (drifted) fragments are merged as written, with a warning. The release commit must then reach `main` (merge the release branch, or cherry-pick it): until it does, the next release refuses rather than release the same fragments twice. The fragment format, including how to re-seal a hand edit and the explicit no-notes state, is `RELEASE-NOTES.next/README.md`.

### Spec lifecycle commands

Use after brainstorming produces a design spec to track formal specifications through implementation:

```bash
# Generate formal specs from a design doc
/doc-superpowers spec-generate --design-doc=docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-14-feature-design.md

# Inject spec compliance tasks into a plan
/doc-superpowers spec-inject --phase=plan --plan=<path> --specs=<paths>

# Track spec freshness during execution
/doc-superpowers spec-inject --phase=execute --specs=<paths> [--plan=<path>]

# Verify spec compliance before merging
/doc-superpowers spec-verify --mode=post-execute --specs=<paths> --design-doc=<path> [--plan=<path>]

# Check spec coverage during code review
/doc-superpowers spec-verify --mode=review --changed-files=<paths>
```

Each path in `--specs` takes an optional role suffix — `--specs=<path>:target`, `--specs=<path>:constraint`, or `--specs=<path>:amends` (the plan corrects what the spec *says* without building its surface; status-neutral, verified as landed — pass `--plan=<path>` to `spec-verify` so the check can confirm the amendment cites the plan). An explicit marker always wins; unsuffixed paths stay valid and have their role inferred at execution time, and inference never yields `:amends`.

**Spec claims (opt-in).** A project that creates `docs/spec-claims/` turns its specs' and ADRs' normative sentences into executable claims, checked by `doc-tools.sh claims <verb>`: `spec-generate` writes stub claims, `spec-inject --phase=plan` adds a claims gate to each chunk and a final gate, and the git hooks and the `doc-spec-verify` / `doc-freshness-schedule` workflows run the same checks. Without that directory every `claims` verb is inert and nothing above changes. See `references/spec-claims.md`.

Opting in changes more than the spec actions:
- **Commits.** With git hooks installed, the pre-commit claims leg blocks a commit on a claims finding whatever `DOC_SUPERPOWERS_STRICT` says. `DOC_SUPERPOWERS_CLAIMS_SKIP=1` skips that leg alone (`DOC_SUPERPOWERS_SKIP=1` skips the whole hook). The pre-push leg only reports.
- **Pull requests.** The PR claims job is part of `doc-spec-verify`, an opt-in AI workflow: install it by name (`hooks install --ci --workflows=doc-spec-verify`) to have every same-repository PR checked. The weekly schedule, a default workflow, re-runs the claims either way.
- **Adapters.** A `test` claim runs through a runner adapter you write and name in `docs/spec-claims/config.json` (`runners`, which defaults to `{}`); without one, every check of that claim is indeterminate (exit 2), never a pass.
- **`--plan`.** Pass `spec-verify --mode=post-execute --plan=<path>`: its claims verdict (`claims attest --plan <plan> --final`) needs the plan, and without it the run reports "claims verdict owed", never PASS. It also writes `final.json`, so commit first: the final gate refuses a dirty tree.

### Work ledger (opt-in)

If you track work as markdown issue files (`docs/issues/*.md`) — or as GitHub issues — the work ledger gives each item a stable key, generates ledger pages from the items, finds related work through named contracts, and warns when another branch or machine touches what yours depends on. It is off until `docs/ledger/config.json` exists (`{}` is a complete config): without it every `doc-tools.sh ledger` verb except `init` prints `ledger: not enabled (no docs/ledger/config.json)` and exits 0.

Bootstrap it on a repository that already has issues (or let `/doc-superpowers init` run it as its *Ledger (opt-in)* step):

```bash
# 1. A report, a registry proposal and a decisions file — nothing else is written
$DOC_TOOLS ledger init --report /tmp/ledger-init.md [--registry <file>] [--sources files,github]
# 2. Edit docs/ledger/ledgers.proposed.json and fill the decisions column of /tmp/ledger-init.md.decisions.tsv
# 3. Apply exactly what you decided: config, registry, keys, item fields, legacy.json
$DOC_TOOLS ledger init --accept /tmp/ledger-init.md.decisions.tsv --dry-run
$DOC_TOOLS ledger init --accept /tmp/ledger-init.md.decisions.tsv
```

Everyday verbs:

```bash
$DOC_TOOLS ledger ls --ledger checkout --open      # one line per item
$DOC_TOOLS ledger show checkout-14                 # one item in ≤ 25 lines
$DOC_TOOLS ledger new --ledger checkout --summary "Totals round twice on refunds"   # a key for a new issue
$DOC_TOOLS ledger note checkout-14 "repro on staging"                              # the one home for item state
$DOC_TOOLS ledger view all --html --open           # render the views locally
$DOC_TOOLS ledger validate --all                   # every item, the registry, keys
```

Exit codes are the claims family: 0 ok, 1 findings, 2 could not run, 3 usage. With the ledger on, `spec-inject --phase=plan` also pastes a `## Related work` sweep into the plan and adds a `Ledger notices (chunk N)` gate to each chunk. Config keys, keys and provisional keys, adapters, the in-flight layer (it publishes local branch names to the remote: read the privacy note first) and the hooks are in `references/ledger.md`.

For wrapper skill integration details, see `references/spec-lifecycle-protocol.md`.
For code review and commit review integration, see `references/integration-patterns.md`.

## All Available Commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `/doc-superpowers init` | Generate full doc suite from scratch |
| `/doc-superpowers audit [scope]` | Full documentation health check |
| `/doc-superpowers review-pr` | PR-scoped doc review |
| `/doc-superpowers update [scope] [--report=<path>]` | Execute doc updates from an audit report (default: this session's audit, else the freshness check) |
| `/doc-superpowers diagram [scope]` | Regenerate architecture and workflow diagrams |
| `/doc-superpowers sync` | Sync doc index with filesystem |
| `/doc-superpowers hooks install [--git] [--claude] [--ci] [--all] [--ledger] [--ledger-claude] [--workflows=<csv\|all\|none>] [--force] [--base-branch NAME] [--cron EXPR] [--ci-strict[=true\|false]]` | Install workflow hooks (CI: the shell workflows by default, the rest by name; choices recorded; the ledger sets opt-in, never in `--all`) |
| `/doc-superpowers hooks status [--git] [--claude] [--ci] [--all] [--ledger] [--ledger-claude]` | Show installed hooks |
| `/doc-superpowers hooks uninstall [--git] [--claude] [--ci] [--all] [--ledger] [--ledger-claude] [--workflows=<csv\|all\|none>] [--transient]` | Remove installed hooks (granular CI uninstall; `--transient` keeps state non-intentional) |
| `/doc-superpowers spec-generate --design-doc=<path>` | Generate formal specs from design doc |
| `/doc-superpowers spec-inject --phase=plan\|execute --specs=<paths> [--plan=<path>]` | Inject spec tasks into the plan (`--plan` required) or track drift after a chunk |
| `/doc-superpowers release [--from=<ref>]` | Draft release notes entry from git history |
| `/doc-superpowers ledger <verb> [args]` | The work ledger (`doc-tools.sh ledger <verb>`; inert without `docs/ledger/config.json`, except `init`) |
| `/doc-superpowers spec-verify --mode=post-execute\|review --specs=<paths> [--plan=<path>]` | Verify spec compliance (`post-execute` also takes `--design-doc=<path>`; `review` takes `--changed-files=<paths>`, with `--specs` optional) |

## Verification

After running `init`, verify the output:

1. Check that `docs/` contains the expected structure (the list follows the *Scope → Generated Docs Matrix* in `skills/doc-superpowers/SKILL.md`):
   - `architecture/system-overview.md` (always)
   - `architecture/diagrams/` (always)
   - `architecture/{component}.md`, one per major component (if `application` scope detected)
   - `specs/README.md` + `template.md` (always)
   - `adr/README.md` + `template.md` (always; in the project's existing `docs/decisions/` when it keeps its ADRs there)
   - `workflows/{name}.md` for the primary workflow (always)
   - `workflows/diagrams/` (always)
   - `workflows/agentic/README.md` + `workflows/agentic/{skill}.md` per skill (if `agentic` scope detected)
   - `guides/getting-started.md` (always)
   - `codebase-guide.md` (always)
   - `conventions.md` (always), with a `## Testing` section (if `testing` scope detected)
   - `## Packages` sections in `architecture/system-overview.md` and `codebase-guide.md` (if `monorepo` scope detected)
   - `plans/`, `archive/` (created later, when a report, plan or archived doc is first written there)
   - `api-contracts.md` (if `api-contracts` scope detected)
   - `data-layer.md` and `architecture/diagrams/erd.png` (if `data-layer` scope detected)
   - `ci-cd.md` and `workflows/deployment.md` (if `ci-cd` scope detected)
   - `infra.md` (if `infrastructure` scope detected)
   - `.doc-index.json` (always)

2. Each generated file except `template.md` should start with the doc-superpowers marker (freshness itself is recorded in `docs/.doc-index.json`; a `template.md` carries no marker, so a spec or ADR copied from it does not inherit one):
   ```
   <!-- Generated by doc-superpowers -->
   ```

3. Review the generated content against your project — the skill uses evidence-based verification but human review is the final gate.

4. Check hooks status (if installed):
   ```bash
   /doc-superpowers hooks status
   ```
   This reports which hook tiers are installed and their current state.
